subject.declared_domain: The comp-tool family (NFRA_COMP*): `comp-trace <node> [--direction up|down|both] [--depth N] [--json]` traces data paths through the full stack on the head-pinned TRACE graph (gold scripts + functions, lambdas, S3 artifacts, endpoints, eventbridge rules, portal components). Declared in comp-tools.yaml:224, graph-call-manifest.yaml and .tools/tool_index.py:935 (canonical_call `comp-trace <node> --direction both [--depth N]`). The subject is an 8-line bash SHIM: it resolves the workspace from its own location, execs `python org/modules/graph/cli.py trace "$@"`, captures the exit code, runs the auto-logger comp_log_auto.py under `2>/dev/null`, and exits with the tool's code. Everything a user experiences as comp-trace lives in cli.py (1,584 lines) and trace_graph.py; the card qualifies the shim AND the contract it delegates, reading across the exec per the card-5 lesson.

as_of.graph_vintage: The shim's last change is ea7a7c99f8 (2026-07-09, 2.0.0_SA_COO~B) -- the same commit as its two sibling shims comp-iam and comp-platinum (subjects 3 and 4 of this face), all three the one 8-line template. Its dispatch target cli.py moved most recently at the 2026-08-04 'comp-trace dial' (T1/T3/T6 in the source); comp_log_auto.py last moved 2026-07-30 (R8, the sink change). The substrate it serves is the trace-graph CACHE .comp-graph/graph.json (gitignored): at carding it carried built_at 1786056515 = 2026-08-05T20:08:35Z with 2,249 nodes / 2,947 edges, and trace_freshness() read STALE -- 375 of 1,904 indexed nodes had source-SHA drift (25 days of unrebuilt cache); the carding EXERCISE rebuilt it (see process.methodology).

methodology.how: FOUR LINES OF BEHAVIOUR (.tools/comp-trace:4-8): (1) WORKSPACE derived from the shim's own path (`cd $(dirname $0)/..`), so the tool is location-derived, not device-hardcoded (the LD-0405 rule met by construction); (2) `python $WORKSPACE/org/modules/graph/cli.py trace "$@"` -- every argument forwarded intact; (3) `_exit=$?` captured; (4) `python comp_log_auto.py "comp-trace" "$*" $_exit 2>/dev/null` -- the run logged with the args COLLAPSED to one string ($*, not $@) and the logger's stderr DISCARDED; (5) `exit $_exit` -- the tool's code, not the logger's, is what the caller sees. THE DELEGATED CONTRACT (cli.py, read at :95-130, :214-262, :354-410): _get_graph() serves .comp-graph/graph.json when no indexed node has source-SHA drift, else prints STALE_NODE_WARN to stderr, DISCARDS the drifted cache and REBUILDS head-pinned from current source (47.7 s at carding, 2,303 nodes / 3,047 edges), saving the new cache -- so a trace run is also a cache WRITE whenever anything drifted; cmd_trace() prints a provenance banner (cache path, built_at, age, sha-drift at load) to stderr on EVERY walk (T3), resolves the query by prefix (or byte-equal id under --exact, T6), and on zero matches exits rc=3 LOUD with the denominator, the universe and near-matches printed (T1) -- never a silent rc=0 clear. EXERCISED at carding: `.tools/comp-trace gold:A_00.accounts_dimension --exact --direction down --depth 1` -> STALE_NODE_WARN (375 drifted, ten listed, '... and 365 more'), rebuild, banner 'built_at=2026-08-30T13:12:42Z (age 0.8min); sha-drift at load: 375 of 1930', results, rc 0; and the run landed as a row in the live sink (see cadence).

persistence.form: TWO artifacts per run. (a) stdout: the trace (text, or a JSON object under --json with query/matches/status/denominator/universe/near_matches_unverified on NOT-FOUND); stderr: the provenance banner + any STALE_NODE_WARN / rebuild lines. (b) SIDE EFFECTS: the trace-graph cache .comp-graph/graph.json REWRITTEN whenever drift is found (g.save, cli.py:108) and one row APPENDED to org/mcp/comp-tool-runs.jsonl by the logger (ts_epoch, serial, to_id, tool, args_head, rc, result, session_id, verdict_basis, and the R8 route_id/route_age_s/route_n when a comp-which route was handed off). The shim itself persists nothing; both writes are the delegate's and the logger's.
persistence.evidence: cli.py:106-108 (build_graph + g.save(_CACHE_FILE) on the rebuild path); the exercise's banner showing the new built_at; comp_log_auto.py:347 (runs_sink = org/mcp/comp-tool-runs.jsonl) and the observed last row after the exercise. 'projection': the trace is a read of a graph that is itself a projection of the working tree (head-pinned at build). 'replaceable': the cache is fully rewritten on rebuild (atomic save per the :99 comment on the closed C1 reap window); the sink is append-only but is the LOGGER's artifact, not this tool's.
persistence.owner: cache: whoever rebuilds (any comp-trace/comp-blast/comp-build caller); sink: comp_log_auto.py's (AE_CloudComp class, R8)

coverage.universe: The head-pinned TRACE graph: 2,303 nodes / 3,047 edges after the carding rebuild (2,249 / 2,947 in the 08-05 cache), of which 1,930 indexed nodes carry a source SHA (1,904 before). A query covers the nodes whose ids match it (prefix by default, byte-equal under --exact) and the edges reachable within --depth in --direction.
coverage.denominator: PRINTED ON THE PATH THAT NEEDS IT: a NOT-FOUND prints the node count and the per-type breakdown ('denominator: N nodes (HEAD-PINNED TRACE GRAPH) -- FUNCTION=..., SCRIPT=...') plus the universe statement and near-matches (cli.py:385-407); the provenance banner prints indexed-node drift as 'k of N' on every walk. NOT printed: on a successful match, how many nodes the graph holds OUTSIDE the walked depth -- a --depth 1 answer does not say what depth 2 would have added. The run logger records args_head only (the first ~60 chars of the collapsed args), so the sink cannot reconstruct a long invocation.
explicitly_out: AWS config planes (IAM / SG / DNS / ...) and the silver tier -- 'ask comp-kuzu / comp-blast for those' (:397-399)

any node the builder did not index -- a file type or path root outside build_graph's scan roots is absent from the universe and a query on it reads NOT-FOUND (loud, rc 3), never 'nothing depends on it'
the deployed plane: the graph is built from the WORKING TREE ('PLANE: repo working tree', the banner's own words); a deployed artifact whose source diverged is invisible

the logger's stderr: the shim's `2>/dev/null` on :7 discards the COMP_LOG_AUTO_DROP last-resort disclosure, so when the marker file .comp-graph/.comp_log_drops is also unwritable a dropped run row is silent after all (the logger's docstring promises the opposite)
coverage.evidence: Node/edge counts from the tool's own rebuild line and the cache file; the NOT-FOUND denominator block read at cli.py:378-407 and exercised indirectly (the 9 rc-3 rows in the sink are that path firing for real callers); the `2>/dev/null` at .tools/comp-trace:7 against comp_log_auto.py:45-69 (_disclose_drop: marker file -> stderr -> bare pass) -- the shim removes the middle rung. .comp-graph/.comp_log_drops did NOT exist at carding (`ls` -> no such file): either no drop has ever occurred or the marker write has never fired; the two are byte-identical from outside, and the stderr rung that would separate them is the one the shim discards.
coverage.owner: the shim (this card's subject) for the discarded stderr; cli.py for the universe statement

key.identity_space: Graph node ids: prefixed strings ('gold:<script>.<function>', 'lambda:<name>', 's3:<key>', endpoint / eventbridge / component ids) built by trace_graph.build_graph from the working tree; the run sink keys rows by (ts_epoch, serial, session_id) with `verdict_basis` naming the rc-to-result mapping vintage ('derived@v1+<hash>').
key.key_expression: QUERY RESOLUTION: g.find_node(query) = prefix match over node ids (:359); under --exact, `m.id == query` byte-for-byte (:365) -- a miss under --exact is rc 3, never a silent widening. FRESHNESS KEY: per-node source_sha vs the current file's sha (check_node_freshness) -- content-addressed, not mtime. LOG KEY: tool + collapsed args + 30 s window (the dedup key .comp-graph/.comp_dedup 'timestamp|dedup_key'). ARGS RENDERING: `"$*"` joins with single spaces, so `comp-trace 'a b'` and `comp-trace a b` log identically while resolving differently.
key.declared_mapping: The id prefixes and the universe are declared in the NOT-FOUND text and the banner; the prefix-vs-exact split is declared in --help and the T6 comment. NOT declared anywhere on the shim: that the logger sees `$*` while the tool sees `$@`; nor that stderr from the logger is discarded. The registry entry for THIS tool is .tools/tool_index.py:1295-1305 (id trace.walk.dependency_chain): canonical_call 'comp-trace <node> --direction both [--depth N]', cost '~ms warm', freshness 'graph.json (5-min TTL)', rebuild_trigger 'new files -> comp-build', mode 'query-cached'. Two of its three declared fields are FALSE against the code: cli.py:214-217 states the default path has NO TTL (TRACE_PREDICATE = 'content-SHA drift per indexed node (no TTL on the default path)'), so 'graph.json (5-min TTL)' describes a freshness model the tool does not run; and 'new files -> comp-build' is not the only rebuild trigger -- any SHA drift on an indexed node rebuilds inside comp-trace itself (47.7 s at carding), so '~ms warm' is the cost only while nothing has drifted. (An earlier cut of this card cited :1515 -- comp-estate's entry -- for the cost line; that was a transplanted citation, corrected at the certifier's STOP.)
key.evidence: cli.py:359 (find_node), :365 (--exact), :214-217 (the predicate), :326-352 (banner); comp_log_auto.py:141-178 (dedup key and window); the shim's :5 vs :7 quoting; tool_index.py:935 canonical_call and the cost/freshness metadata strings (the ~0.3s figure read there). Rated STABLE: node ids are deterministic functions of paths/names and the sha key is content-addressed; the instability is in the RENDERING the logger receives, recorded under failure_mode.
key.owner: cli.py / trace_graph.py for the id space; the shim for the args rendering; tool_index.py's cost line is the registry's

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: THE TOOL: LOUD in every measured branch. NOT-FOUND -> rc 3 with denominator + universe + near-matches (the 'false-clear fix', 3.0.0_SA_CVO 2026-06-26, T1 2026-08-04); a corrupt/truncated cache -> WARN to stderr + rebuild (the C1 reap window closed by the atomic save; the WARN added so a real load bug is not hidden behind a slow rebuild); drift -> STALE_NODE_WARN listing ten drifted nodes and the count, then rebuild; the rc histogram in the sink (27 x 0, 9 x 1, 9 x 3, 2 x 120) shows the loud paths firing for real callers. THE SHIM: propagates the tool's exit code exactly (:6, :8) and never masks it with the logger's; the ONE thing it silences is the logger (:7 `2>/dev/null`), whose only failure output is the drop disclosure. THE LOGGER: never raises into the tool by design ('never disrupts the calling tool'); on any error it discloses to the marker file, else stderr (discarded by the shim), else passes.
silent_degrade_paths: a dropped run row when the marker file is unwritable: the logger's stderr disclosure is discarded by the shim's `2>/dev/null`, so the run vanishes from the sink with no trace -- the freshness/health signal the logger's docstring says must not undercount invisibly, undercounting invisibly

a cache that never drifts is served at any age (no TTL on the default path) -- correct by the predicate, but a 25-day-old cache that happened to be un-drifted would read 'fresh' with nothing to say so except the banner's built_at

a trace run on a drifted cache silently costs a 47.7 s rebuild and a ~1.5 MB write that the registry's '~ms warm' cost line (tool_index.py:1297) does not mention, under a freshness model ('5-min TTL', :1298) the code does not run; the caller sees the rebuild only on stderr
the logged args are `$*`-collapsed and truncated to args_head: an invocation with quoted whitespace or a long argument list is not reconstructible from the sink
a successful walk does not print the size of the universe it did not walk (depth beyond --depth), so a --depth 1 'clear' can read as complete
failure_mode.evidence: Exit-code propagation read at :6/:8 and exercised (rc 0 returned through the pipeline). The loud NOT-FOUND read at cli.py:366-410 and evidenced by the 9 rc-3 sink rows. The drop-disclosure chain read at comp_log_auto.py:45-69 and the shim's redirect at :7; .comp-graph/.comp_log_drops absent at carding (never fired, or never written -- indistinguishable, as stated under coverage). 'yes' on distinguishable: for the TOOL's own verdicts a typo, an out-of-universe subject and a genuine no-dependents are three different outputs (rc 3 with near-matches / rc 3 with the universe statement / rc 0 with an empty result), which is exactly what T1 was built to separate; the 'no' cases above are the LOGGER's and are bounded to the run record, not the trace.
failure_mode.owner: the shim (this seat's family, 2.0.0_SA_COO~B) for the discarded stderr and the $* rendering; cli.py's authors for the tool's branches; the registry's cost line: tool_index.py's

verdict.why: As a shim it does the four things a shim must: derives its workspace from its own path (device-agnostic by construction), forwards every argument intact, propagates the tool's exit code without masking, and logs the run without ever disrupting the tool -- exercised end to end at carding, rc 0, the run row observed in the live sink. The tool it delegates to is the loudest instrument in this face: a NOT-FOUND prints its denominator, universe and near-matches at rc 3; a drifted cache is announced and rebuilt; a corrupt cache is announced and rebuilt; the provenance banner prints both vintage axes on every walk. QUALIFIED on three measured points that belong to the shim or to the contract as declared. FIRST: line 7's `2>/dev/null` discards the logger's stderr, and the logger's stderr is its LAST-RESORT drop disclosure -- so when the marker file cannot be written, a lost run row is silent after all, which is the exact undercount the logger's 2026-07-10 amendment was written to end; the marker file did not exist at carding and the shim is why that absence cannot be read. SECOND: the logger receives `$*` while the tool receives `$@` -- the recorded command is a rendering, not the invocation, and args_head truncates it further. THIRD: the registry's contract for this tool (tool_index.py:1295-1305) declares cost '~ms warm', freshness 'graph.json (5-min TTL)' and rebuild_trigger 'new files -> comp-build'; against the code, the default path has NO TTL (cli.py:214-217, the tool's own comment), freshness is per-node SHA drift, and any drift rebuilds inside comp-trace itself -- a 47.7 s rebuild and a ~1.5 MB write on the call that hit it; the cache was 25 days old with 375 of 1,904 nodes drifted at carding, so nothing but a caller's drift triggers a refresh, and the tool ran once in the prior 14 days while the estate committed hundreds of times behind the Rule 20 gate it is named in. None of these produce a wrong trace; all of them make the run record or the cost incomplete relative to what is declared.
blocking_defects: the shim's `2>/dev/null` on the logger call (.tools/comp-trace:7) discards comp_log_auto.py's stderr, which is the logger's last-resort drop disclosure (:66-67) -- a dropped run row is silent when the marker file is unwritable, contrary to the logger's stated invariant (coverage + failure_mode rows)

the logger is handed `"$*"` while the tool is handed `"$@"` (:5 vs :7): the logged command is a whitespace-collapsed rendering, then truncated to args_head -- not reconstructible for quoted or long invocations (key row)

the registry contract for comp-trace (tool_index.py:1295-1305: cost '~ms warm', freshness 'graph.json (5-min TTL)', rebuild_trigger 'new files -> comp-build') is false on two of three fields against cli.py:214-217 (no TTL on the default path; freshness = per-node SHA drift; drift rebuilds inside comp-trace) and omits the rebuild cost: 47.7 s + a cache write on the call that hits drift -- the cache was 25 days / 375-of-1,904-nodes stale at carding (cadence + key rows)

Rule 20's 'before every cloud/infra/data/frontend change' rhythm has no mechanism (comp-surface-check retired): 47 runs since 07-25, one in the 14 days before carding, against hundreds of gated commits -- the declared rhythm is not the live one (cadence row; the rhythm is CLAUDE.md's, not the shim's)
